rationale: The ground truth's only substantive concerns are Gaohan123's P1 (does the live 501/message mapping for level-2 wake really hold, or does it contradict the PR's own '500' framing) and P2 (the CPU mock test only proves route propagation, not the real engine contract) — both later resolved via yenuo26's explanation of an upstream NotImplementedError→501 handler and an agreed rename. Y independently re-derives and confirms exactly that resolution (citing vLLM's app.exception_handler(NotImplementedError) and create_error_response mapping) and separately flags, almost verbatim, that the mocked test 'tests route propagation, not the engine contract' and proposes a stubbed-orchestrator unit test — matching the human thread closely. X only loosely brushes P1 (confirms the 501 mapping as an already-verified fact, without engaging the PR-description contradiction) and never raises P2 at all. Both candidates independently converge on several of the same non-ground-truth bugs (vacuous VRAM assertions, exception-swallowing _ensure_awake, AMD CI redness), cross-validating precision for both at a similar level; Y's findings are slightly more actionable, with explicit 'Change:' code-level fixes and verified command output (pytest --collect-only, local 16-passed run).
